title: Claim identity includes row position, page URL, capture digest, fetch date and OSM version, so an identical fact re-mints as a new claim when its row moves or is re-captured; each re-mint is a new independence class
evidence: content_digest = sha256 of the whole claim dict minus claim_id/sys_period/recorded_at; dot_511 evidence dict carries source_url (paged resultOffset URL) and Locator.row(feature_index). Probe (uv run, CameraRegistryEntry.claim_rows + db.claim_sink.content_digest): moving only feature_index 7->8 changed the digest of all 8 claims; changing only the page URL did the same. An upstream deletion shifts later rows, so unchanged facts are inserted again instead of recording a re-sighting; with NEW-4 the duplicates count as separate classes (U3/U8 in reconcile/resolve.py:910-916,1005-1016).

title: The predicate and genre vocabulary is open at the sink: an unregistered predicate is auto-registered with generic defaults and then silently dropped by the resolver, so the fact is stored but never resolved, corroborated or contradicted
evidence: _REGISTER_PREDICATES inserts any new predicate as MODERATE/365/authoritative_source_wins; UNKNOWN_PREDICATE is raised only on the intake path (intake_apply.py:484). Unregistered predicates emitted today (verified): installation_date, last_checked, upstream_ref (osm_tag_vocab.toml:58-60), portal_stated_permitted_use (flock_portal_vocab.toml:86), deployed (pathways.py:536), retention_window_observed (data_driven.py:653). Atlas stamps non-registry genres (atlas_vocab.toml:56-65: osint, news_reporting ...); OSM and Eyes on Flock stamp none (fallback connector_run D3 instead of osm_node_set D2 / portal_snapshot D1). The resolver raises KeyError -> 'no directness row' and drops the claim.

title: Subject keys collide or drift: Legistar contract keys are not tenant-scoped, Atlas and EFF agency keys omit the state, and camera keys take the first matching id alias (server row ids when nothing else matches) with no uniqueness check, producing silent merges that have no match record
evidence: contract:{source}:{external_id} with source 'legistar' spanning agenda tenants; atlas:{raw agency name}:{family}; data_driven:agency:{name}; camera key = first alias hit in a global list (CAMERAID ... id, Id, ID, rowid, OBJECTID, FID ...), not pinned per target and never checked for uniqueness. Alias resolution over dot_511_targets observed_fields: dot_511_il keys on OBJECTID. A key collision merges two real things into one entity outside ER, violating SIG-IDENT-025 ('an unexplainable merge is a violation'). Magnitudes need a spine query (L2).

title: Independence is never declared in production: the PG readers never set independence_class, derived_from_source or collection_method, so every claim is its own independence class and SIG-RECON-018 ('never per claim') is unmet in practice; the same reader also drops valid_period and declared directness
evidence: class_id = independence_class or derived_from_source or claim_id; method = collection_method or source_id or claim_id. grep over connectors/db/reconcile/resolution/inference/exports finds no producer; the only setter is one unit test. The reader selects no valid_period, so _intersects_world is always true and same-source supersession collapses period-specific values to 'latest wins'. SIG-EPIS-009 (derived_from_claim_ids) and SIG-EPIS-029 (undeclared-copying detector; only a constant at reconcile/model.py:59) are MET-DIFFERENTLY in the matrix but absent in code. Extends ED-49/F2b NEW-2.

title: Every connector subject is typed 'deployment' in the entity table, including agencies, contracts, portals and bills, so APIs serve agencies as deployments and accountability anchors treat contracts and agencies as deployments
evidence: _DEFAULT_ENTITY_TYPE = 'deployment' is used for every sig.connector.subject ref; only object refs carry a declared type. Live corroboration from earlier rows: K12b cites /v1/entity/deployment/... for the Austin PD sharing subject; I1 NEW-4 cites /v1/entity/deployment/01a0bd32... for an Eyes on Flock portal. No test asserts subject entity type.

title: Two overlapping DeFlock/OSM republishes registered as targets of one source (camreg_osm_surveillance) can never be deduplicated: the same-source hard constraint forbids it and the duplicate-target exception needs row- or byte-identical captures; 13,724 excess rows share coordinates to 0.1 m
evidence: DuckDB over the C3 sha-verified osm_physical.parquet, source_id='camreg_osm_surveillance' (154,528 rows): groups with >1 row at round(lat,6),round(lon,6) = 13,529 groups / 27,253 rows / 13,724 excess; at 5 dp 14,436 excess. OSM nodes rarely coincide to 1e-6 deg, so these are overlapping republishes (inference). Counted separately in the observation-level figures and the 'unresolved' bucket.

title: The camera ER's ALPR-vs-traffic incompatibility guard is keyed on source-id and operator substrings, so the largest ALPR layer (camreg_osm_surveillance) is classed 'unspecified' and is compatible with traffic cameras; any source id containing 'dot' or 'its_' is classed traffic
evidence: device_class checks source_prefixes/source_substrings (flock, alpr, lpr; dot_511_, dot, 511, traffic, its_), operator substrings, then camera_type; the rules file notes no hosted camera_type value matches the ALPR type rule. Root cause is I1 NEW-9 (no technology predicate); this is its consequence inside ER.

title: No cross-source deduplication reaches any published record: camera-site ER output is used only for one national count, no cluster id is exported and entity.merged_into has no writer, so 2,933 points published by two or more sources add 5,016 excess rows to dossiers, the map and bulk files
evidence: read_resolved_site_runs feeds only resolved_sites_metric (N of M). grep: merged_into is read (accountability.py:401) but never written. DuckDB over the 11 compartment parquets (distinct entity_id/source/jurisdiction/point): 2,933 ~1 m cells with >=2 sources, 7,949 rows, 5,016 excess (PA 1,861; MD 1,101; GB-ENG 562; KY 414; NZ 298); top pairs camreg_penndot_pa+camreg_ucsd 923, camreg_mark43+camreg_nottingham_gb 558. 'Resolved' also means different things in §28, the export envelope, camera ER (latest claim) and coverage. Materially changing published counts is HG-11 (ADR-101 §4).

evidence: json census: 540 pairs; adjudicators agent:claude-opus-5-5@sig-maintainer-seed x540 and llm:claude-opus-5-5@camera-rules-v1-blind x540 (kappa 0.669 is model-vs-model); verifier labels 403 match / 3 non_match / 134 NEI; frozen holdout 180 = 150 match / 30 NEI / 0 non_match; strata cross_source_mirror 95 of 180; top holdout source pairs camreg_mark43 x camreg_nottingham_gb 28, camreg_osm_surveillance x camreg_stanford_us 18, camreg_caloes_ca x camreg_trafficops_ca 15. wilson_lower_95 is computed but decide_auto_write_tiers gates on precision_strict. Extends C3 NEW-4 / F2b NEW-3 / F4 NEW-5.

title: The sharing-edge seam loses time and provenance: undated claims become 1970-01-01 edge start dates, materialized edges are never superseded, every edge is 'ongoing' with no currency, the export and the materializer use different classifiers and different edge sets, and asymmetry is inferred from the mere absence of the counterparty's export
evidence: read_sharing_observations uses c.observed_at only and substitutes date(1970,1,1); edge_row sets valid_to_kind 'ongoing' always and valid_period lower = observed date; read_materialized_edges has no upper_inf(sys_period) filter; support hard-coded WEAKLY_SUPPORTED/evidence_count 1 (260 claims -> 130 edges); shaping classifier matches bare 'use' and lacks 'sharing_partner'; sharing_edges.csv comes from the compute-on-read set credited to SIG; EFF 2016-17 data stamped with a config constant 2020-01-28; network node labels looked up in source_names (entity UUID never matches). Root causes for K12b NEW-1/NEW-2.

title: The 5,290 'conflicted' subjects in the 2026-09-27 release are an artifact of pre-P32.4 code that treated every same-source claim as a concurrent candidate; the chain tip will silently resolve them to the latest value at the next republish, hiding key instability such as IDOT's OBJECTID-keyed layer
surface: db/src/db/occurrences.py:295-316; exports/src/exports/shaping.py:874; reconcile/src/reconcile/resolve.py:555-576; commit 18bda164 (2026-09-27T06:41Z) vs release Last-Modified 2026-09-27T01:33:43Z
evidence: At b051732c envelope candidates are the latest claim per source (key source_id or claim_id), so a single source can no longer conflict; the release predates that commit. IDOT (2,936 of 3,000 conflicted) is the one DOT target whose key resolves to OBJECTID (alias resolution over observed_fields). If its conflicts come from server row-id reassignment (hypothesis), the subjects now denote different cameras over time and 'latest wins' conceals it. Needs INV-05 key-stability monitoring before the next republish.

title: There is no production organisation entity resolution: organisations are exact scoped-name keys that are never unioned, the Splink matcher only enqueues proposals to an unstaffed queue, run_entity_resolution has no production caller and the UEI/LEI crosswalk path is fed by no connector, so the accountability join (operator = contract buyer) cannot fire
evidence: ADR-122 §3 keys sig.org.name_scoped as jur:<j>|<name> or src:<source>|<name>, never auto-unioned; the six production materializers omit org ER; ADR-099 §1 describes materializing cascade+Splink outputs, but materialize_resolutions writes §28 value decisions. candidate_identifier/jurisdiction_candidate/resolved_entity_id keys are never read under db/. The hosted export shows 0 dossiers with a governance chain (sub-agent read of L2 captures; consistent with C3 §4.6).

title: Release validation checks integrity only (hashes, undeclared files, key uniqueness per compartment, index counts); no truth invariant (geometry in jurisdiction, labels present, duplicates across sources/compartments, edge dates, one 'resolved') runs in CI or the release path, and no test carries one dataset from connector to export
evidence: validate_release has no semantic checks; the e2e steps are not chained (S4 inserts orgs by hand, S7 exports from a hand-written request at :263); hypothesis tests exist only for temporal invariants and sensitivity; every seam is fixture-verified and none is verified against real data by an automated check. This row proposes 17 invariants (L1 §6.2) for L2/L3 and B4 G10.

title: Value mapping is lossy: dict and list values are stored as Python repr strings, units and currencies are dropped or put in non-standard keys, and vendor and type are hard-coded constants
evidence: value_text = str(value) for non-scalar values and no connector sets value_json; EFF retention unit goes to retention_unit, not unit; vendor 'Vigilant Solutions (LEARN)' is a config constant; OSM persists raw_value without the normalized kind; procurement amount is a string without currency (sub-agent trace, spot-checked). Cross-source numeric comparison (§28 U4, §29 counts) cannot work on these fields.
